# Pinned npm release triage

The supplied Babylon agent 1.1.52, imgbundle 1.0.2 and CodeSift MCP
0.15.5 archives are benign. Babylon installs agent resources and exposes an
optional authenticated bridge; its user service requires an explicit command.
CodeSift provides indexing/MCP tools, opt-out anonymous telemetry, client setup
and optional service management. imgbundle copies a caller-selected file; its
cdn-img-fetch 1.0.4 dependency exports a caller-invoked HTTPS download helper.
Neither import starts a payload download or executable.

Neutral capability and configuration observations move from objective leaves
to the corresponding micro-behavior leaves. Archive co-occurrence of an install
hook and service registration code does not demonstrate a reachable unwanted
persistence operation. Product/member names are not evidence of maliciousness
or safe grounds for suppressing behavior. Name-only image-loader verdicts and
broad product suppressors were removed.

The new markup-button leaf is for action labels, rather than phishing intent.
A voicemail lure requires additional context beyond an ordinary Play label.
Startup executable paths and telemetry variable references remain notable;
neither alone proves malicious persistence or tracking.

Controls cover relocated capabilities and nearby nonmatches: RegExp.exec,
source-code prose, and an audit-cache filename. PNG controls use a documentation
host instead of the existing fixtures' nonexistent-domain exception, so the
content-level decryption/write/detached-execution rule is exercised. Extraction
without execution and execution without a PNG carrier reject that rule. These
fixtures are static input only and must not be executed. cases.json records
verified report-level expectations.

The dispatch leaf was audited for duplicates before relocating these additions.
Close-event callback registration and a bare named-function call are distinct
from computed dispatch; they use event-callback and direct-call sibling leaves.
The bare exec identifier does not establish child-process execution.
